## Goal

Represent the map and player independently of keyboard input and rendering.

## Files

- `gridworld/models/tile.py`
- `gridworld/models/level.py`
- `gridworld/models/player.py`

## Tasks

- Complete the supplied methods without changing their public signatures.
- Load and validate the JSON map; report file, JSON and map validation errors through `LevelError`.
- Build `floor`, `wall` and `exit` tiles, keeping `levels/n0.json` unchanged.
- Provide grid queries, player position updates and independent `LevelState` and `EntityState` dictionaries.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] N0 is 7 × 5, with start `(1, 1)` and exit `(5, 1)`.
- [ ] Walls are blocked; floor and exit tiles are walkable. An unknown tile kind raises `ValueError`.
- [ ] An invalid map raises `LevelError`.
- [ ] `get_tile(x, y)` raises `IndexError` outside the grid, including negative coordinates; `is_walkable` and `is_exit` return `False` outside the grid.
- [ ] Moving the player does not change the level's starting position. Player does not decide whether a move is allowed.
- [ ] `Player.to_state()` returns a new dictionary with exactly `id="player-1"`, `kind="player"`, `x`, `y` and `appearance="player"`.
- [ ] Exported states are JSON-serializable. Changing their dictionaries or nested lists does not change the models.

## Evidence

In a reviewed PR linked to this issue, record manual checks for loading N0, walls, the exit, out-of-bounds coordinates, invalid maps and independent snapshots. Demonstrate the results and explain the model responsibilities to the tutor at the start of S1.

Use manual checks in S0. Automated tests begin in S1.
Organize the work and peer reviews within your group.
